articles.title: Welcome to MIMS
articles.summary: A quick orientation to the Medical Information Management System.
articles.content_html:
What is MIMS?

MIMS (Medical Information Management System) is a unified platform for managing medical information cases, content, and communications across your organisation.

Who uses it?

  • Case Agents — log and process medical information requests.
  • CM Admins — manage approved documents, FAQs, templates, and merge reports.
  • Org Admins — configure the system, products, workflows, and users.
  • Superadmin — manage organisations and platform-wide settings.

How to get started

  1. Log in with your assigned email and password.
  2. Your home screen shows the modules you have access to.
  3. Use the top navigation bar to move between modules.

What happens next?

Click the ? button at the bottom-right of any screen to get contextual help for that feature.

articles.title: Navigating the Platform
articles.summary: How to use the top navigation bar, sidebar, and module switcher.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The navigation bar at the top of every page gives you quick access to your modules, notifications, and account settings.

When to use it

Use the nav bar to switch between Cases, Content, Browse, Reports, and Admin sections.

How to do it

  • Click a module name in the top bar to navigate to it.
  • The bell icon opens your notification feed.
  • Your avatar/initials in the top-right opens account options and logout.

What happens next?

The page refreshes to the selected module. Your current work is not lost unless you navigate away mid-form.

articles.title: Cases Overview
articles.summary: What cases are and how they flow through MIMS.
articles.content_html:
What is a Case?

A case is a record of a medical information request — a question from a healthcare professional, patient, or internal stakeholder about a product. Every case has a unique case number, status, and owner.

When to use it

Create a case any time you receive a new medical information inquiry that needs to be tracked, responded to, and archived.

How to do it

  • Click + New Case from the Cases list.
  • Fill in the case type, priority, product, and contact details.
  • Assign an owner and submit.

What happens next?

The case moves to Open status. The assigned agent receives a notification and can begin processing the inquiry.

articles.title: Case Statuses Explained
articles.summary: Understand each case status: Open, In Progress, Pending, Closed.
articles.content_html:
What are case statuses?

Statuses show where a case is in its lifecycle and who needs to act next.

Status definitions

  • Open — Case created, not yet being processed.
  • In Progress — Agent is actively working on the response.
  • Pending — Waiting for additional information from the requester or third party.
  • Closed — Response delivered and case archived.

How to change status

Open the case detail and use the Update Status dropdown. Some transitions require a note or e-signature.

What happens next?

Status changes are logged in the case audit trail and may trigger notifications to the assigned user or case owner.

articles.title: Creating a New Case
articles.summary: Step-by-step guide to logging a new medical information case.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The New Case form lets you capture all details about a medical information request in a structured, compliant format.

When to use it

Use this whenever a new inquiry arrives — by phone, email, or in person — and needs to be tracked in MIMS.

How to do it

  1. Click + New Case from the Cases module.
  2. Select Case Type (Medical Information, Adverse Event, Product Complaint, etc.).
  3. Choose Priority and the relevant Product.
  4. Add at least one Contact under the Contacts tab.
  5. Assign the case to an agent.
  6. Click Save.

What happens next?

The case is created with a unique case number. The assigned agent sees it in their queue and receives a notification.

articles.title: Case Detail Page Guide
articles.summary: How to use the case detail view: tabs, actions, and history.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Case Detail page shows all information about a single case — the main record, contacts, medical information, adverse events, product complaints, and full audit history.

When to use it

Open a case detail any time you need to view, update, or close a case.

How to do it

  • Click any case number in the Cases list to open its detail page.
  • Use the tabs at the top to navigate between MI, Contacts, AE, PC, and Audit sections.
  • Use the action buttons (Update Status, Assign, Close) in the header area.

What happens next?

All edits are logged with the editor's name and timestamp. The case audit trail is immutable and 21 CFR Part 11 compliant.

articles.title: Managing Case Contacts
articles.summary: How to add, edit, and manage contacts on a case.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Case contacts are the people connected to a medical information request — the requester, healthcare professional, patient, or caregiver.

When to use it

Add a contact when you have someone whose details should be recorded against the case (required for most case types).

How to do it

  • Open the case and click the Contacts tab.
  • Click + Add Contact.
  • Fill in name, role, email, and phone.
  • Mark one contact as Primary if needed.

What happens next?

The contact is saved against the case. Their details can be referenced in merge reports and correspondence templates.

articles.title: Medical Information (MI) Section
articles.summary: Recording medical information details within a case.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The MI section captures the specific medical information request — the product, question category, and details of the inquiry.

When to use it

Fill in the MI section for any case where the requester has a specific medical or scientific question about a product.

How to do it

  • Open the case and click the MI tab.
  • Select the Product and MI Category.
  • Enter the Question and any relevant notes.
  • Click Save MI.

What happens next?

The MI record is linked to the case and contributes to product inquiry analytics on the Reports page.

articles.title: Adverse Event (AE) Reporting
articles.summary: How to log and manage adverse event details within a case.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The AE section records adverse events reported within a case — product safety events that may require regulatory reporting.

When to use it

Capture AE information any time a contact reports a suspected adverse reaction to a product during a case interaction.

How to do it

  • Open the case and click the AE tab.
  • Click + Add Adverse Event.
  • Enter the event description, onset date, severity, and outcome.
  • Link to the relevant contact.

What happens next?

The AE is recorded and may trigger a regulatory submission workflow depending on your organisation's configuration.

articles.title: Product Complaint (PC) Reporting
articles.summary: Recording product quality complaints within a case.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The PC section captures product quality complaints — issues relating to the physical product rather than a clinical adverse event.

When to use it

Use the PC tab when a contact reports a packaging defect, labelling issue, or product quality concern.

How to do it

  • Open the case and click the PC tab.
  • Click + Add Complaint.
  • Select complaint type and enter description, lot number, and expiry date if available.

What happens next?

The complaint is linked to the case and feeds into product quality analytics.

articles.title: Case Workflow & Assignments
articles.summary: Understanding how cases are assigned, escalated, and closed.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Cases flow through a defined lifecycle — from creation through processing to closure — with assignments, notifications, and audit entries at each step.

When to use it

Understand workflow when you need to reassign a case, escalate it, or complete it.

How to do it

  • To reassign: Open the case, click Assign, and select a new agent.
  • To escalate: Change the case priority to High or Critical from the detail header.
  • To close: Click Close Case from the status dropdown. A note is required.

What happens next?

Assignments and closures are logged in the audit trail. The previous and new owners receive notifications.

articles.title: Content Folders
articles.summary: How folders organise your content library.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Folders are the top-level containers in the Content Management module. Every document, FAQ, template, and merge report lives inside a folder.

When to use it

Create folders to organise content by product, therapy area, country, or document type — whatever structure works for your team.

How to do it

  • Go to Content → Folders tab.
  • Click + New Folder.
  • Enter a name, select a product, and save.

What happens next?

The folder appears in the folder panel of all content tabs (Documents, Modules, FAQs, etc.) and in the Browse Content module for agents.

articles.title: Managing Documents
articles.summary: Uploading, versioning, and publishing approved documents.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Documents are the primary content assets in MIMS — product monographs, prescribing information, clinical summaries, and other approved reference materials.

When to use it

Upload a document when you have a new or updated approved resource that agents should be able to access and reference in case responses.

How to do it

  1. Go to Content → Documents tab.
  2. Select the folder in the left panel.
  3. Click + New Document.
  4. Upload a file (PDF, Word, etc.) or paste HTML content.
  5. Fill in name, category, keywords, and version.
  6. Click Save.

What happens next?

The document is created in Draft status. Use Publish to make it available to agents in the Browse Content module.

articles.title: Document Versioning & Checkout
articles.summary: Using checkout/checkin to safely edit published documents.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

MIMS uses a checkout/checkin system to prevent conflicting edits. When a document is checked out, only the checkout owner can edit it.

When to use it

Check out a document before making edits to an existing published or draft document.

How to do it

  • Find the document and click Checkout.
  • Make your edits and upload the new file.
  • Click Checkin with an optional change note.

What happens next?

A new version entry is created in the document's version history. The minor version number increments automatically (e.g. 1.0 → 1.1).

articles.title: Bulk Document Actions
articles.summary: How to publish or archive multiple documents at once.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Bulk actions let you Publish or Archive multiple documents in one step, saving time when managing large content libraries.

When to use it

Use bulk actions after a product update to publish a batch of new documents, or to archive outdated materials.

How to do it

  • Go to the Documents tab.
  • Select the checkboxes next to the documents you want to act on.
  • Click Bulk Actions → Publish or Archive.
  • Confirm the action in the popup.

What happens next?

All selected documents update to the new status. Archived documents are hidden from agents but remain in the system for audit purposes.

articles.title: Content Modules
articles.summary: What modules are and how they differ from documents.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Modules are reusable content blocks — chunks of structured text that can be referenced in multiple documents or templates. Think of them as building blocks for larger content.

When to use it

Create a module when you have content (e.g. a safety statement, dosing table, or indication summary) that appears in several different documents.

How to do it

  • Go to Content → Modules tab.
  • Click + New Module.
  • Enter a name, paste or type the HTML content, and save.

What happens next?

The module is available in the Browse Content module for agents, and can be referenced from templates.

articles.title: Response Templates
articles.summary: Creating and using letter/email templates for case responses.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Templates are pre-approved letter and email templates that agents use to draft responses to medical information inquiries. They support merge fields that automatically fill in case data.

When to use it

Create a template for any type of response your team sends frequently — e.g. standard MI response letters, acknowledgement emails.

How to do it

  1. Go to Content → Templates tab.
  2. Click + New Template.
  3. Select the template type (Response / Transmission / Correspondence).
  4. Write the content using HTML. Insert merge fields like {{case_number}}, {{patient_name}}.
  5. Save and publish.

What happens next?

Agents can use the Render action to fill merge fields with live case data and generate a ready-to-send document.

articles.title: Template Merge Fields Reference
articles.summary: List of all supported {{merge_fields}} and what data they pull.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Merge fields are placeholders in templates that are replaced with real data when a template is rendered for a specific case.

Supported merge fields

  • {{case_number}} — unique case ID
  • {{case_type}} — type of case (MI, AE, PC)
  • {{case_status}} — current status
  • {{case_priority}} — priority level
  • {{case_assigned_to}} — assigned agent's full name
  • {{patient_name}} — primary contact full name
  • {{patient_email}} — primary contact email
  • {{product_name}} — product from MI record
  • {{org_name}} — organisation name
  • {{agent_name}} — logged-in user's name
  • {{date}} — today's date (long format)
  • {{report_name}} — template/report name

How to use

Type the field exactly as shown (double curly braces, no spaces) inside your template HTML. Fields that don't resolve are left as-is.

What happens next?

When you click Render/Generate, all fields are replaced with live data from the selected case.

articles.title: Merge Reports
articles.summary: Creating and generating merge report templates from live case data.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Merge Reports are document templates — similar to templates but specifically designed to generate structured reports by merging case data into a formatted layout.

When to use it

Use merge reports to generate consistent, pre-formatted reports for individual cases — e.g. a case summary PDF for submission or archiving.

How to do it

  1. Go to Content → Merge Reports tab.
  2. Click + New Merge Report and choose a folder.
  3. Write or paste your HTML content with {{merge_fields}}.
  4. Click ⚡ Generate from the action menu.
  5. Enter the Case ID to pull live data.
  6. Preview, then download as HTML or print to PDF.

What happens next?

The generated output is saved against the merge report record. It can be regenerated at any time for a different case.

articles.title: FAQs Management
articles.summary: Creating, approving, and expiring frequently asked questions.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

FAQs are approved question-and-answer pairs that agents can reference or send to requesters. They follow a draft → approved → expired lifecycle.

When to use it

Create FAQs for common medical questions about your products. They appear in agents' Browse Content module for quick reference.

How to do it

  1. Go to Content → FAQs tab.
  2. Click + New FAQ.
  3. Enter the question, answer, category, and an expiry date.
  4. Submit for approval.

What happens next?

The FAQ goes to Pending Approval status. An approver must e-sign it before it becomes visible to agents. FAQs auto-expire on the set date.

articles.title: FAQ Approval Workflow
articles.summary: How the e-sign approval process works for FAQs.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

FAQs require electronic signature approval before they are published to agents. This ensures compliance with content governance policies.

When to use it

When a FAQ is submitted for approval and you are an authorised approver.

How to do it

  • Find the FAQ with Pending Approval status.
  • Click Approve.
  • In the e-sign modal, enter your password and a confirmation note.
  • Click Confirm Approval.

What happens next?

The FAQ moves to Approved status and becomes visible in the Browse Content module. The approval is logged with your signature in the audit trail.

articles.title: Content Reviews
articles.summary: Scheduling and tracking periodic content review cycles.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Reviews section manages scheduled review cycles for your content library — ensuring documents, FAQs, and templates are regularly checked for accuracy and compliance.

When to use it

Set up a review when a document or FAQ is published, or when a regulatory deadline requires periodic content validation.

How to do it

  • Go to Content → Reviews tab.
  • Click + New Review.
  • Select the content item and assign a reviewer.
  • Set the due date and any notes.

What happens next?

The reviewer receives a notification. When they complete the review, they can approve or flag the content for update. Review status is tracked on this screen.

articles.title: Browse Content
articles.summary: How to search and access approved documents, FAQs, and modules.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Browse Content module is the agent-facing library of all approved reference materials — documents, content modules, FAQs, and templates.

When to use it

Use Browse Content when you need to find reference information to answer a case, or to locate a document to send to a requester.

How to do it

  • Click Browse in the top navigation.
  • Use the search bar to find content by title or keyword.
  • Filter by folder, type, or status using the dropdowns.
  • Click a card to open the detail sidebar.
  • Switch to the Preview tab to view the file inline.

What happens next?

You can download the file, copy the content, or reference the document in a case note.

articles.title: Previewing Documents & Modules
articles.summary: How the inline document and module preview works.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Browse Content detail sidebar has a Preview tab that lets you read documents and modules without downloading them.

When to use it

Use preview to quickly check a document's content before deciding to use or download it.

How to do it

  • Click any document or module card in Browse Content.
  • In the detail sidebar, click the Preview tab.
  • For HTML content, the document renders in an inline frame.
  • For PDFs, the file opens in the browser's built-in PDF viewer.
  • For images, the image is displayed directly.

What happens next?

You can download the file using the link at the bottom of the preview pane, or close the sidebar to return to the list.

articles.title: Reports & Analytics
articles.summary: Overview of available reports and how to generate them.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Reports module provides analytics and exports for cases, content, and compliance activities across your organisation.

When to use it

Use reports for periodic case volume reviews, regulatory submissions, team performance tracking, or content usage analytics.

How to do it

  • Click Reports in the top navigation.
  • Select the report type from the left panel.
  • Apply date range and filter options.
  • Click Generate to load the data.
  • Use Export to download as CSV or PDF.

What happens next?

Generated reports are not saved automatically. Download or screenshot the results if you need to retain them outside MIMS.

articles.title: Inbox & Notifications
articles.summary: How the MIMS notification inbox works.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Inbox shows all system notifications directed to you — case assignments, status changes, approval requests, and system alerts.

When to use it

Check your inbox regularly to stay informed of actions that require your attention.

How to do it

  • Click the bell icon in the top navigation to open the notification overlay.
  • Or go to Inbox in the navigation for the full list.
  • Click a notification to navigate to the relevant case or record.
  • Mark notifications as read individually or in bulk.

What happens next?

Read notifications remain in your inbox for 30 days, then are automatically cleared. Unread notifications persist indefinitely.

articles.title: Managing Picklists
articles.summary: How to add, edit, and reorder dropdown values across MIMS.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Picklists define the dropdown options used throughout MIMS — case priorities, types, categories, contact roles, and more. Admins control what values appear in these dropdowns.

When to use it

Edit picklists when you need to add a new option, rename an existing one, or deactivate values that are no longer relevant.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Picklists.
  • Select the picklist type from the left panel.
  • Click + Add Item to add a new value.
  • Use drag handles to reorder, or click the edit icon to rename.
  • Toggle the active switch to deactivate without deleting.

What happens next?

Changes take effect immediately. Deactivated values no longer appear in dropdowns but existing records that used them are unaffected.

articles.title: Field Setup & Custom Fields
articles.summary: Configuring which fields appear on case and contact forms.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Field Setup lets admins control which fields appear on case forms — making fields required, optional, hidden, or adding custom fields unique to your organisation.

When to use it

Use Field Setup when you need to capture additional information in cases that isn't in the default form, or to hide fields that aren't relevant to your workflow.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Field Setup.
  • Select the form (Case, Contact, MI, AE, PC) from the top tabs.
  • Toggle fields between Required, Optional, and Hidden.
  • Click + Add Custom Field to create a new field.

What happens next?

Form changes apply to all new cases immediately. Existing case records are not affected.

articles.title: Workflow Activities
articles.summary: Configuring workflow stages and transition rules for cases.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Workflow Activities define the steps a case goes through — what statuses are available, what transitions are allowed, and whether a note or e-signature is required.

When to use it

Configure workflow when you need to add a new case status, change who can transition a case, or enforce documentation at a specific step.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Workflow.
  • Select the case type from the dropdown.
  • Add, edit, or reorder workflow steps.
  • For each step, set: allowed roles, required note, and e-sign requirement.

What happens next?

The updated workflow applies to new and in-progress cases. Agents will see only the transitions allowed for their role at each step.

articles.title: Product Dictionary
articles.summary: Managing your product and brand list in MIMS.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Product Dictionary is the master list of products (medicines, devices, etc.) that can be referenced in cases, MI records, and content.

When to use it

Add a product when a new drug or device needs to be tracked in MIMS, or update an existing product when its details change.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Product Dictionary.
  • Click + Add Product.
  • Enter the brand name, INN (international non-proprietary name), therapeutic area, and active status.

What happens next?

The product becomes available in case MI forms, content folder assignment, and reporting filters.

articles.title: Security Groups & Permissions
articles.summary: How security groups control what each user can see and do.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Security Groups define role-based access control for your organisation — which modules users can see and what actions they can perform.

When to use it

Use security groups when onboarding new users with specific access requirements, or when you need to restrict access to sensitive case types or content.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Security Groups.
  • Click + New Group or edit an existing one.
  • Toggle permissions for each module (Cases, Content, Reports, etc.).
  • Assign users to the group from the Users section.

What happens next?

Users see only the modules and actions permitted by their security group. Changes take effect on next login.

articles.title: Case Numbering Configuration
articles.summary: Setting up automatic case number formats for your organisation.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Case Numbering lets you define the format for automatically assigned case numbers — e.g. MI-2026-00001.

When to use it

Configure case numbering when setting up a new organisation or changing your numbering convention.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Case Numbering.
  • Select the case type.
  • Set the prefix, year format, separator, and padding.
  • Click Save.

What happens next?

New cases created after saving use the new format. Existing case numbers are not changed.

articles.title: Organisation Management
articles.summary: How superadmins create and manage organisations and sites.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Organisations section (Superadmin only) is where new pharmaceutical organisations and their sub-sites are created and managed within MIMS.

When to use it

Use this when onboarding a new client organisation, adding a site/subsidiary, or deactivating an organisation.

How to do it

  • Go to Superadmin Console → Organizations.
  • Click + New Organisation.
  • Enter the name, contact details, and select which modules to enable.
  • Add sites under the organisation if needed.

What happens next?

The organisation is created. You can then set up users, assign admins, and configure module access for the org.

articles.title: Content Intelligence — Overview
articles.summary: Introduction to the four AI-powered content analysis features.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Content Intelligence is a suite of AI-powered tools in the Admin Console that help you analyse, validate, and manage the quality of your content library.

The four features

  • Evidence Chain — traces the source evidence behind content claims.
  • Contradiction Radar — identifies conflicting statements across documents.
  • Digital Twin — creates a regulatory profile snapshot for a product.
  • Adaptive Risk — scores the regulatory risk of your current content state.

When to use it

Use Content Intelligence during content audits, before regulatory submissions, or when reviewing newly uploaded materials.

What happens next?

Each tool generates an analysis report viewable on screen. Results are not automatically acted upon — you review and take action based on the findings.

articles.title: Evidence Chain Analysis
articles.summary: How to trace the scientific evidence behind a content claim.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

Evidence Chain traces how a claim in your approved content is supported by source evidence — clinical studies, product labels, and regulatory documents.

When to use it

Use Evidence Chain when you need to verify that a claim is backed by current, valid evidence — e.g. before publishing new content or responding to a regulatory query.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Content Intelligence → Evidence Chain.
  • Select the document or enter a content claim.
  • Click Analyse.

What happens next?

The system returns a chain of evidence nodes showing supporting sources, confidence levels, and gaps where evidence is missing or weak.

articles.title: Policy Graph
articles.summary: Visualising and managing your medical affairs policy relationships.
articles.content_html:
What is this?

The Policy Graph is a visual map of your medical affairs policies — showing how internal policies, SOPs, regulations, and content interconnect.

When to use it

Use the Policy Graph to understand the impact of a regulatory change on your existing policies, or to identify policy gaps before an audit.

How to do it

  • Go to Admin → Policy Graph.
  • Click + Add Node to add a policy or regulation.
  • Draw connections between related nodes.
  • Use Evaluate to run an impact analysis from a selected node.

What happens next?

The graph updates in real-time. The evaluate function returns a risk propagation report showing which downstream policies are affected by a change at the selected node.
